scenes.teacherScript: Welcome to the masterclass on Magnetic Effects of Electric Current. Here is what this video covers. First: how a current-carrying wire makes a compass needle move. Second: magnetic field lines around a magnet and a wire. Third: the solenoid and the electromagnet. Fourth: Fleming's left hand rule for force on a conductor. Fifth: electromagnetic induction with a magnet and a coil. And finally: the electric motor versus the generator. Let us get started!

content.title: Oersted's Discovery
content.subtitle: Current flowing through a wire makes a compass needle move!

scenes.teacherScript: In 1820, Hans Christian Oersted discovered something shocking. He placed a compass needle near a wire carrying current, and the needle MOVED! Electric current creates magnetism. This is the magnetic effect of electric current. Let us understand it, step by step.

content.title: Magnetic Field & Field Lines
content.subtitle: Closed loops from North to South, never crossing.

scenes.teacherScript: A magnet creates a magnetic field around it, an invisible region where it attracts or repels. We draw this field using field lines. The lines start at the NORTH pole, curve around, and enter the SOUTH pole. Inside the magnet they go from south to north, so field lines form CLOSED LOOPS. Two field lines NEVER cross. Where the lines are close together, the field is strong. Where they spread out, the field is weak.

content.title: Current in a Straight Wire
content.subtitle: Concentric circles around the wire, direction by the Right Hand Thumb Rule.

scenes.teacherScript: Now let's understand the direction of the magnetic field around the wire, step by step, with our right hand. Step one: the right hand thumb rule. First, always check the direction of the CURRENT. Here, the current is flowing UP the wire. So point your right thumb UP, just like the current. Now curl your fingers. Your curled fingers show the direction of the MAGNETIC FIELD. And see, they curl ANTI-clockwise. So: current UP, thumb UP, field ANTI-clockwise. Step two: now the current flows DOWN. First check the current, it is DOWN. So point your thumb DOWN, just like the current. Curl your fingers again. They show the field direction. And now they curl CLOCKWISE. So: current DOWN, thumb DOWN, field CLOCKWISE. Remember: first check the CURRENT, the THUMB follows the current, and the FINGERS show the FIELD.

content.title: The Solenoid
content.subtitle: Uniform, strong field inside, behaves like a bar magnet.

scenes.teacherScript: A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated wire. When current flows, the fields of all the turns COMBINE into one much stronger field. Inside the solenoid, the field lines are straight, parallel, and close together, so the field inside is UNIFORM and STRONG. Outside, the pattern looks exactly like a bar magnet. One end behaves like a NORTH pole, and the other end behaves like a SOUTH pole.

content.title: The Electromagnet
content.subtitle: Soft iron core + solenoid = magnetism you can switch ON and OFF.

scenes.teacherScript: Wrap the solenoid around a SOFT IRON core and you get an ELECTROMAGNET. Current ON, it becomes a strong magnet and picks up iron pins. Current OFF, the magnetism DISAPPEARS and the pins drop. That is the special trick: electromagnets can be switched ON and OFF. That is why cranes use them to lift scrap iron, and doorbells use them too.

content.title: Force on a Conductor
content.subtitle: Fleming's Left Hand Rule: Field, Current, Force.

scenes.teacherScript: Let's do the classic experiment. Take a conductor between the poles of a strong magnet. The magnetic field goes from the NORTH pole to the SOUTH pole, here, UPWARD. Now pass a current through the conductor, INTO the page. Watch, the conductor experiences a FORCE, and it MOVES. It moves to the LEFT. Reverse the current, OUT of the page, and the conductor moves to the RIGHT. The force is strongest when the current is at RIGHT ANGLES to the field. The direction of this force is given by FLEMING'S LEFT HAND RULE. Stretch the thumb, the first finger and the middle finger of your LEFT hand, all mutually perpendicular. The FIRST finger points in the direction of the FIELD. The MIDDLE finger points in the direction of the CURRENT. The THUMB points in the direction of the FORCE, the motion of the conductor. Field, Current, Force, three fingers, all at right angles to each other.

content.title: Electromagnetic Induction
content.subtitle: A moving magnet in a coil induces current (Faraday).

scenes.teacherScript: Now the reverse: can magnetism create electricity? Yes, this is ELECTROMAGNETIC INDUCTION, discovered by Michael Faraday. Push the magnet INTO the coil, the galvanometer needle DEFLECTS. Hold the magnet still, the needle returns to zero. Pull the magnet OUT, the needle deflects the OTHER way. Electricity is induced only while the magnet is MOVING, while the field lines are CUTTING the coil. This is the principle of the electric generator.

content.title: Board Exam: Motor vs Generator
content.subtitle: Motor: current in, motion out. Generator: motion in, current out.

scenes.teacherScript: Board question: the ELECTRIC MOTOR converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. It uses the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. The GENERATOR converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. It uses electromagnetic induction. Motor: current IN, motion OUT. Generator: motion IN, current OUT. Remember, MOTOR gives you MOTION.
